title: Repeated String Match
statement: Writing `a` out `q` times back to back gives a longer string (zero copies give the empty string). Return the smallest `q` for which `b` appears as a contiguous substring of that string, or `-1` if no number of copies ever contains `b`.
constraints: a and b contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force keeps appending `a` and asks whether `b` has appeared yet. Two facts make one scan enough. First, the repetition of `a` is periodic, so if `b` occurs at all it occurs starting inside the first copy of `a`; such a match ends before index `a.length + b.length`. Second, the fewest copies are needed by the occurrence that ends earliest. So run the Knuth–Morris–Pratt matcher for `b` over the endless text `a a a ...` (read with `i % a.length`, never built), and the first full match gives the answer.

## Approach

1. Build `failure` for `b`: `failure[i]` is the length of the longest proper prefix of `b` that is also a suffix of `b[0..i]`.
2. Walk text positions `i` from `0` to `a.length + b.length - 1`, reading `ch = a[i % a.length]`.
3. While `ch` does not extend the current match, fall back with `matched = failure[matched - 1]`; then extend if it fits.
4. When `matched` reaches `b.length`, the match ends at `i`, so `ceil((i + 1) / a.length)` copies are needed.
5. If the scan ends with no match, return `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`a = "abcd"`, `b = "cdabcdab"`; `failure` is `[0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`. The text reads `abcdabcdabcd...`. Positions 0–1 (`a`, `b`) match nothing; from `i = 2` the letters `c d a b c d a b` match `b` one by one, so `matched` hits 8 at `i = 9`. The answer is `ceil(10 / 4) = 3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m): the failure table costs O(m) and the scan covers `n + m` positions, each fallback paid for by an earlier step forward.
- Space: O(m) for `failure`; the repeated text is never stored.

## Pitfalls

- Stopping at `ceil(b.length / a.length)` copies is one short: `b` may start late in the first copy and need one more.
- Count copies from where the match ends, `ceil((i + 1) / a.length)`, not from `b.length` alone.
- A short `b` inside one copy of `a` needs just 1 copy, even when `b` is shorter than `a`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `failure` | KMP table: longest prefix of `b` that is also a suffix ending at each index |
| `length` | current prefix length while the table is being built |
| `limit` | number of text positions worth scanning, `a.length + b.length` |
| `i` | position in the endless repetition of `a` |
| `ch` | the letter at that position, `a[i % a.length]` |
| `matched` | how many letters of `b` currently match, ending at `i` |

narration.11: Record the longest border ending at position i.
